_comment: Spawn template for a daemon inside a docker container. Merge the templates block into ~/.omp/orchestrator/config.json (or point OMP_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG at this file after editing). ENROLL: 1) build/push your ompd image and set OMPD_IMAGE (or edit docker-ompd.sh's IMAGE default); 2) edit the wrapper path below to the absolute path of orchestrator/examples/docker-ompd.sh in your repo checkout. Then `omp-orchestrator spawn <path> --template docker`. The wrapper publishes the container's 4721 onto a random host port and prints an OMPD| endpoint line with the published URL, which the orchestrator's endpoint resolver prefers (R6b) — so it always dials a reachable address. The workspace is bind-mounted at its HOST path so the daemon reports the same cwd the orchestrator registered (hello_ok cwd sanity check); if your docker cannot bind the exact path, adjust the mount AND --cwd in the wrapper together. SECURITY — dial-in only: the container never dials out and holds no orchestrator credentials; the bearer token (minted per spawn, passed on the container command line) gates ONLY this daemon — the --host 0.0.0.0 bind is a startup hard error without it. The token is visible via `docker inspect` to anyone who can reach the Docker socket: restrict Docker socket access. The token also rides the host process list briefly (single-operator v1 tradeoff, README Phase 6).
